# Playbook: Clone-and-Rebrand

A working product — the user's own, or one already rebuilt under the Clone / Rebuild playbook — keeps its functionality, data, and users, and gets a completely new identity: name, brand, design language, voice and copy, domains, and search presence. Nothing about what the product *does* changes. Everything about what it is *called, looks like, sounds like, and is found as* does — in one coordinated pass, because a half-finished rebrand is worse than none: two names in the wild split search equity, confuse users, and leave the old brand legally and operationally alive in places nobody remembered to look.

> **The legal line, which governs every step below: function may be cloned; protected expression may not be copied.** This playbook keeps the product's function and replaces its identity — so the new name, design language, voice, and copy must be original expression authored for this product, never copied from a third party's product, and never a continuation of protected expression the product had no right to carry. Where the product being rebranded is itself a clone, clone-ethics' authorization record and LG-186/LG-187 decide what may carry over at all.

## Goal

Ship the product under its new identity with zero unapproved old-brand residue anywhere a user, a search engine, a mail server, or a lawyer can find it: rendered pages, assets, metadata, structured data, emails, notifications, legal documents, app-store and directory listings, social profiles, and the codebase's user-visible strings. Carry the old identity's search equity across deliberately — a complete one-to-one redirect map from old URLs to new, the old domain kept alive and redirecting, sitemaps and canonicals pointing only at the new identity — and prove both halves (no residue, no lost routes) with scans and crawls, not by inspection. Functionality, user accounts, and data are untouched: if a change would alter behavior, it is not part of this playbook.

## Departments + order

Step 0 (always-on core) → **D14 pre-flight (rights and clearance only)** → D1 → D9 (baseline + surface inventory) → **rebrand-execution (anchor, D16 — loaded at step 3, executed at step 4)** → D3+D13 → D4+D11+D18 (touchpoints) → D14 (full) → D9 (seo-migration) → D7+D8 → D6 → D9+D12+D18 (cutover verification, monitoring, announcement)

**Order deviations, and why.** Three, all forced by the mission:

1. **D14's clearance pre-flight runs before D1**, not in its usual post-build position, because a new name that fails trademark/domain clearance after design work has started burns the entire design step. Clearance is cheap at step 1 and expensive at step 6.
2. **D9 runs twice, at both ends.** Up front it captures the SEO baseline and the brand-surface inventory while the old identity is still fully live — after cutover, the old state can no longer be measured. At the end it executes the migration (redirects, sitemaps, canonicals) and verifies continuity. A rebrand that inventories after it redesigns will miss surfaces, and one that measures rankings after it switches cannot prove what the switch cost.
3. **D6 (domains/DNS) runs before the final D9 verification, not as the last build step**, because the redirect map can only be proven against the real new domain with real certificates. The announcement (D18) is the actual last step, and it waits for that proof.

There is deliberately **no D2/D5 build step**: no new architecture and no schema change. D4 appears only as a touchpoint step (user-visible strings, email and notification templates, metadata the backend emits) — handlers, contracts, and data stay exactly as they were. If the commission also asks for new features or a rebuild, that work runs under its own playbook first; this playbook starts from a working product and ends with the same product, renamed.

## Docs to write first

Before any identity work, scaffold from `project-templates` and write:

The full mandated set for this type is `templates/mandated-manifest-clone-and-rebrand.txt`, which governs (G-PM-001); the list below is the hand-written starting subset, not the whole set.

- `requirements.md` — the rebrand's scope in both directions: what changes (name, marks, palette, type, voice, domain, handles) and what explicitly does not (functionality, data, accounts, pricing, contracts). The not-list is the scope-control instrument for the whole run.
- `fact-sheet.md` — the old identity's verified facts (current name, domains, handles, listings, legal entity name as it appears in existing documents) and the new identity's, each with its source. The clearance checks in step 1 read from here, not from memory.
- `brand-surface-inventory.md` — every place the old identity exists, produced in step 3 but with its file and classification scheme agreed before the audit starts: routes and templates; static assets and filenames (logos, favicons, og images, screenshots, PDFs); metadata and structured data; email and notification templates; legal documents; app-store, directory, and social listings; third-party integrations that display the name (payment descriptors, OAuth consent screens, embedded widgets); documentation and help content; user-visible strings in code. Each row gets an owner step (5, 6, 7, or 8) and a disposition: replace, redirect, retire, or retain-with-reason.
- `old-new-mapping.md` — the single mapping table every later step works from: old name → new name, old terms → new terms (product-specific vocabulary, plan names, feature names if they change), old domain/paths → new domain/paths, old handles → new handles, old asset files → new asset files. Frozen at step 4; a change after the freeze is a `DECISIONS.md` entry and re-triggers the affected scans.
- `redirect-map.md` — drafted in step 3 from the route inventory, finalized in step 8: one row per old URL, its new target, and its type. Written before cutover, never improvised during it.
- `progress.md`, `DECISIONS.md` — session log and decision record.
- `cutover-runbook.md` — the ordered cutover sequence for steps 10–11 with the rollback trigger and the rollback steps (per `rollback`), written before step 9 so verification tests what cutover will actually do.
- `.env.example` — new-domain and mail-domain values by name + purpose (§5.9); sending-domain credentials are secrets and follow the secrets baseline.

## Step-by-step sequence

**Step 0 — Core and scaffold.** Load `bundles/core.md`; generate the project (G-PM-001, G-PM-002); write the docs above; load `secrets-management` before any registrar, DNS, or mail-provider credential is touched.

**Step 1 — D14 pre-flight: rights and clearance before design.** Establish the basis for rebranding at all: the product is the user's own, or the engagement covers identity work (for a cloned product, the Clone / Rebuild playbook's authorization record is the input — read it, do not re-create it). Then clear the *new* identity: trademark and trade-name search in the markets the product operates in, domain availability for the exact name, and handle availability on the platforms in the inventory. Clearance results are recorded in `fact-sheet.md` with sources and dates.
◆ **DECISION — is the new name clear?** A name with a conflicting mark in the product's own category, or whose exact-match domain and primary handles are all taken, does not proceed to design on hope. The options are exactly: pick a different name, or proceed with the conflict recorded and counsel's view noted (G-LG-035's counsel-review pattern). (Unattended run: BOOTSTRAP's approval-points rule applies at this point — a decision recorded in the commissioning brief or `requirements.md` counts as the answer. If none is recorded and no user is reachable, clearance is never log-and-continued and never safe-defaulted: whether a name may be used is a legal position (§6.3 Step 5 never list), and the proceed-with-conflict option requires counsel's view, which an unattended run cannot have. Stop before design, log the blocker in `progress.md` (§6.3 step 3), and ask the user with concrete options (§6.3 step 4). Clearance is the one step whose failure gets more expensive every day it is deferred.)

**Step 2 — Requirements and scope freeze (D1).** requirements-writing turns the commission into the two lists in `requirements.md` (changes / does-not-change); scope-control records the freeze. Name the audiences who must not be surprised: existing users (they will log in to a product that looks and is called something else), search visitors arriving on old URLs, and recipients of already-queued email. Those three audiences set the step 6 and step 11 work.
◆ **DECISION — big-bang or phased identity switch?** Big-bang (one cutover: name, design, domain together) is the default and the only mode this playbook's gates fully prove. A phased switch (name first, domain later, or the reverse) leaves a deliberate mixed-identity period: it requires a `DECISIONS.md` entry naming the interim state, which surfaces carry which identity during it, and the end date — and the residue gates in step 9 are then run against the *interim* mapping, not the final one. (Unattended run: BOOTSTRAP's approval-points rule applies at this point — a decision recorded in the commissioning brief or `requirements.md` counts as the answer; if none is recorded and no user is reachable, follow the §6.3 stuck protocol (log-and-continue, then the safe defaults) and record the substitution in `progress.md`.)

**Step 3 — Baseline and surface inventory (D9, first pass).** While the old identity is still fully live: technical-seo runs the route inventory crawl (G-CO-002) and the redirect and status audit (G-CO-003) on the old domain; web-analytics records the baseline — which routes carry organic landing traffic, which carry none — in `brand-surface-inventory.md`, citing Search Console / analytics evidence per route class, so step 8 can rank redirect-map rows by what is actually at stake. Then the surface audit itself, per the inventory scheme in the docs above: crawl the rendered site, dump the templates and string catalogs, list the asset folders, export the email/notification template set, and enumerate the off-site listings from `fact-sheet.md`. Every old-brand occurrence found becomes an inventory row. **Handoff:** this inventory is the input contract for steps 5–8; a surface discovered after step 8 is a defect in this step, and is logged as one.

**Step 4 — Identity spec and mapping freeze (anchor: rebrand-execution).** The new identity is specified as a buildable artifact, not a mood board: name and its exact spellings/capitalization, logo and mark files, palette, type, voice and terminology (the words the product uses for itself and its actions), and the naming rules for files, handles, and metadata. `old-new-mapping.md` is completed from the spec and the inventory and **frozen**; the rebrand-execution skill's inventory gate (G-CL-701) must pass on the inventory and the mapping before step 5 starts — the skill's remaining gates run at their own phases (G-CL-702, G-CL-703, and G-CL-704 at step 9; G-CL-705 at step 11). **Handoff:** D3 receives tokens-and-type decisions, D9-copy and D13 receive voice-and-terminology, D14 receives the legal name forms, D6 receives the domain list — all from this one document, so the departments cannot drift into slightly different versions of the new name.
◆ **DECISION — what happens to the old identity's assets?** Keep the old domain redirecting (default: indefinitely — it is the redirect map's home and the backlink equity's entry point), keep or release the old handles, keep or retire old-brand content pages. Releasing the old domain while external links still point at it hands those links to whoever registers it next. (Unattended run: BOOTSTRAP's approval-points rule applies at this point — a decision recorded in the commissioning brief or `requirements.md` counts as the answer; if none is recorded and no user is reachable, follow the §6.3 stuck protocol (log-and-continue, then the safe defaults) and record the substitution in `progress.md`.)

**Step 5 — Design language and copy (D3+D13, D9 copy).** design-tokens replaces the token source (palette, type scale, logo-derived values) and design-system re-expresses the components in the new language — tokens first, components second, pages last, so no page carries hand-set values the system does not own (G-FE-021 token build, G-FE-014 token and contrast enforcement, G-FE-011/G-FE-012 design-system acceptance). New marks are checked at favicon and app-icon sizes, not only at hero size. In the same step, copywriting + inclusive-copy rewrite the user-visible copy in the new voice: headlines, onboarding, empty states, errors, and transactional strings, worked from `old-new-mapping.md`'s terminology column (G-CO-053 naming lint — the old name and retired terms are the lint's pattern list; G-AC-091 banned-pattern lint, G-AC-093 glossary conformance). accessibility-audit runs on the re-skinned templates in this step, not after: a new palette is a new contrast surface (G-AC-001, G-AC-005; inherited G-EXP-05, G-EXP-06). **What differs from building new:** the layout, components, and content structure already exist and are not redesigned — a rebrand that quietly becomes a redesign breaks the step 2 scope freeze and invalidates the step 3 baseline.

**Step 6 — Touchpoints (D4+D11+D18).** Every non-page surface in the inventory is rebranded from the mapping table: transactional-email templates (sender name, From domain, headers, footers, legal lines) with mail authentication for the new sending domain proven before cutover (G-IN-061 authentication check, G-IN-064 end-to-end arrival test; G-CO-071/G-CO-072 for lifecycle-email); notifications (sender/app name, icons, copy — G-BE-131 trigger test per template class); help-center and user-onboarding content (names, screenshots, URLs — G-CX-022 UI-label and link audit, G-CX-025 stale-article sweep, where "stale" here means *old-brand*); app-store and directory listings, social profiles, OAuth consent screens, and payment descriptors, each updated or scheduled in the cutover runbook with its owner named. Screenshots are re-shot from the rebranded build — an old-UI screenshot under a new name is residue. **Handoff:** step 6 returns a per-row disposition to the inventory; a row it cannot complete (a listing controlled by a third party, a descriptor with a provider lead time) is escalated into the cutover runbook as a dated follow-up, not left as a silent gap.

**Step 7 — Legal identity (D14, full pass).** legal-documents regenerates terms, privacy, and any DPA/cookie text under the new name and entity details, diffed against the privacy register (G-LG-031 document-vs-register diff) and linted for template residue (G-LG-032 — run with the *old* brand's names and the template's placeholder names both on the pattern list). Check the places legal identity hides outside legal documents: copyright footers, invoice and receipt templates, email legal footers (step 6 owns the templates; this step owns what they must say), cookie-banner text, and the imprint/contact pages. If the legal entity itself is renamed or the product was assigned to a different entity, that fact and its effective date are stated in the documents and the announcement — a product rename and a company rename are different events and must not be blurred. licensing confirms the new marks and any new licensed assets (fonts, imagery) are covered for this use (G-LG-051 license scan).

**Step 8 — SEO migration (anchor: seo-migration, with D9).** The migration is built and tested on staging before any DNS change. seo-migration's gates (G-CO-141–G-CO-145) must pass on the redirect map and the migration plan; the map itself is executed and verified with technical-seo's instruments: every row of `redirect-map.md` is a one-hop 301 (or 308) from the old URL to its named new URL — no chains, no blanket redirect of everything to the homepage, no row without a target (a retired page redirects to its closest live successor or is deliberately answered 410, with the reason on the row). Canonicals, sitemaps (G-CO-091 sitemap audit, G-CO-092 count reconciliation against the route inventory), structured data (G-CO-081 CI schema validation, G-CO-082 markup-vs-visible diff — the Organization entity carries the new name and URL with one stable identity site-wide, inherited G-SCH-04), social/Open Graph tags and images (G-CO-111 tag dump diff, G-CO-112 og:image resolution), and metadata (G-CO-011 metadata lint) are all regenerated for the new domain and name — never find-and-replaced blindly, because titles, og URLs, and JSON-LD `@id`s fail in different ways. Internal links point at new URLs directly; a site that links to its own redirects taxes every crawl. **Handoff:** the tested redirect map and the new sitemap set are frozen artifacts handed to D6 — step 10 deploys exactly these files, and any change after this step re-runs this step's verification.

**Step 9 — Verification (D7+D8).** The residue hunt, run against the rendered build and the shipped string set, not source alone: the brand-residue scan (G-LG-094, applied to this mission — the "source brand" is the product's own old brand, and the approved-reuse list is the inventory's retain-with-reason rows: historical changelog entries, the redirect map itself, and legal version archives are legitimate old-name occurrences; everything else blocks) plus placeholder-scan (G-QA-141 — old name, old domain, old handles, and retired terms added to the sweep patterns for this run) and the naming lint re-run (G-CO-053). Asset-level residue gets its own pass: hash- and filename-level check for old logo files, favicons, og images, and screenshots in the shipped build and the asset manifest. Security pass (G-SE-001 ZAP baseline, 0 critical findings — the surface did not change, but the domain and mail configuration did, and those are security-relevant), and qa-gates (G-QA-111). The anchor skill's own gates run in this step as well: G-CL-702 (residue scan over code, catalogs, rendered HTML, sitemap, email templates, and downloadable assets, with the declared Organization logo URL and favicon fetched and confirmed as the new mark), G-CL-703 (URL and search integrity — the production URL set diffed against the step 3 baseline, every pre-launch URL answering directly or by its approved one-hop migration redirect), and G-CL-704 (functional regression — the critical-flow suite returns identical results before and after the swap, because the change set is identity-only under CL-711). **No cutover until green.**

**Step 10 — Domains and cutover (D6).** In runbook order: domains-dns records for the new domain proven against the record sheet (G-DO-101), registrar posture checked (G-DO-102), mail authentication present (G-DO-103); ssl-certificates live and probed (G-DO-111 external TLS scan, G-DO-112 redirect and HSTS probe); the old domain's redirect configuration deployed from step 8's frozen map; ci-cd (G-DO-001) and hosting (G-DO-071 external production check on the *new* domain, and the same check confirming the *old* domain answers with the expected redirect, not a parked page or an error). Performance budgets re-asserted on the rebranded templates (G-AN-101) — new fonts and hero assets are the usual regression.
◆ **STOP AND ASK — registrar, DNS, and sending-domain changes (§5.9/§6.3).** Transferring a domain, changing nameservers, or switching the production sending domain is hard to reverse inside the propagation window and breaks mail and traffic if wrong; it requires the user's explicit go-ahead, with the rollback steps from `cutover-runbook.md` rehearsed on staging first (G-DO-151). (Unattended run: a go-ahead recorded in the commissioning brief or `requirements.md` for this specific change counts as the answer. If none is recorded and no user is reachable, this point is never log-and-continued and never safe-defaulted — registrar, nameserver, and sending-domain changes are destructive-class actions on the §6.3 Step 5 never list. Log the blocker in `progress.md` (§6.3 step 3), ask the user with concrete options (§6.3 step 4), and make no registrar, DNS, or sending-domain change until the explicit go-ahead exists.)

**Step 11 — Continuity verification, monitoring, announcement (D9+D12+D18, last).** Only after step 10 is green: technical-seo's promotion indexability diff on the new domain (G-CO-001 — no staging directive, no old-domain canonical survives), the redirect and status audit re-run against the *live* old domain (G-CO-003 — every redirect-map row fetched and its status and final target compared to the map), the new sitemaps submitted and the change-of-address / property steps for the new domain completed in the search consoles the product uses, and the coverage review log started (G-CO-005). web-analytics confirms the tracking property reports the new domain under the new name (G-CO-121 tracking-plan diff) and monitoring watches the old domain's redirect traffic, 404s on the new domain, and mail bounce rates through the cutover window. Then, and only then, D18 announces: in-product notice and changelog entry (G-PM-061 changelog format), help-center announcement article, email to existing users from the *new* sending domain explaining the rename, what did not change (accounts, data, billing), and that the old address redirects. support-ticketing is briefed with the mapping table — "is this the same product?" is the predictable ticket, and the answer is scripted from `old-new-mapping.md`, not improvised. The run then closes under the anchor skill's G-CL-705: every third-party surface on the inventory opened in its own console, the step 3 baseline re-checked, and the residue report filed from `brand-surface-inventory.md` — every row `swapped`, `kept by exception` with its reason, or `missed` with a fix date. A rebrand with no residue report is not closed, however clean the cutover looked.

## Failure handling

- **Clearance fails at step 1 (name conflicted or unavailable):** stop before design. The cost of a rename is one step of legal checking; the cost of discovering the conflict at step 7 is steps 4–6 redone under a different name. No "proceed and rename the risky parts" partial pass exists.
- **Residue found at step 9 (G-LG-094 / G-QA-141 hit):** the hit's inventory row reopens and returns to its owning step (5, 6, or 7) as the work order; the scan re-runs over the whole surface class, not just the fixed file — one leftover string in a template family usually means the family was edited by hand instead of from the mapping table. A second hit in the same surface class triggers a full re-audit of that class against `brand-surface-inventory.md` before proceeding. Legitimate historical occurrences are resolved by adding the row to the approved-reuse list with its reason, never by allow-listing the old name globally — a global allow-list silently disables the scan for real residue.
- **Redirect verification fails at step 11 (G-CO-003: chains, loops, wrong targets, rows answering 200 or 404):** fix the map row and its server configuration, re-fetch the full map, not just the failed rows — chain and loop faults are configuration-level and rarely unique. If a class of old URLs has no honest target, the disposition is decided per row (closest successor, or deliberate 410) and recorded; bulk-redirecting the class to the homepage is recorded as a failure of this gate, not a fix for it.
- **Search continuity degrades after cutover (coverage review, G-CO-005):** first check the mechanical causes in order — redirect rows still live, sitemaps submitted and clean, canonicals on the new domain, no robots or noindex leftover from staging (G-CO-001 re-run). Do not "fix" a migration by reverting to the old domain on a traffic dip alone; reversal is a rollback decision under the runbook, taken on evidence of a broken migration (failed redirects, wrong canonicals), not on ranking movement, which the baseline in step 3 exists to interpret.
- **Mixed identity discovered live (old name in an email, a store listing, a payment descriptor):** treat as a step 3 inventory defect: add the surface to the inventory, fix it under its owning step, and re-run step 9's scan for that class. Then record in `progress.md` why the audit missed it, so the next rebrand's inventory scheme inherits the lesson.
- **Cutover breaks production (new domain unreachable, mail rejected, redirect loop on the old domain):** execute `cutover-runbook.md`'s rollback — restore the prior DNS/redirect configuration and the prior build — and record the incident. The old identity stays fully live until a second cutover attempt passes step 9 again; a rebrand is never urgent enough to leave users on a broken domain.
- **Any other gate fails mid-playbook:** fix in the owning department, re-run that gate, record both results in `progress.md`. No gate is waived silently; a waiver needs a `DECISIONS.md` entry, and a waiver on G-LG-094 or the seo-migration skill's gates (G-CO-141–G-CO-145) needs the user's explicit agreement, because those two are the mission.

## Definition of done

- New identity live end-to-end: name, marks, design language, voice, and domain consistent across pages, assets, metadata, emails, notifications, legal documents, listings, and profiles — proven by G-LG-094 and G-QA-141 at zero unapproved hits, with the approved-reuse list naming every legitimate old-name occurrence and its reason.
- Search continuity proven, not assumed: every row of `redirect-map.md` fetched live and matching (status, one hop, target); sitemaps reconciled to the route inventory and submitted; canonicals, structured data, and Open Graph tags naming only the new identity (G-SCH-02/03/04); baseline-vs-after coverage review log open and current (G-CO-005).
- Existing users unharmed and informed: accounts, data, and billing untouched (step 2's does-not-change list verified, not just asserted); announcement sent from the new sending domain with mail authentication passing (G-IN-061, G-DO-103); support briefed with the mapping table.
- Old identity disposed of as decided in step 4: old domain redirecting under the user's ownership, old handles kept or released per the `DECISIONS.md` entry, no old-brand asset still served from the new build.
- All gates above green; `progress.md` shows the full gate trail including the step 3 baseline; `cutover-runbook.md`, `handover.md`, and the inventory are current — the inventory is the next rebrand's starting document.
- **Pre-provisioning complete:** where the new domain or sending domain is not yet provisioned, the project may be recorded as *pre-provisioning complete* when every gate except the provisioning-waived ones (G-DO-071, G-DO-111, G-CO-001, and step 11's live redirect verification) is green, each waived gate is recorded as a provisioning waiver per §6.3, and the unblocking conditions are listed in `progress.md` — the cutover, announcement, and continuity requirements above remain open until the domains exist. A rebrand is not announced on a pre-provisioning build.

## Worked mini-example

Sample project: **Listloop**, a small shared-bookmarking web app (web only, no native apps), renamed to **Shelfmark** with a new domain, because the owner found an unrelated product already trading under a similar name.

1. Step 0: core loaded; project scaffolded; registrar and mail-provider credentials handled under the secrets baseline.
2. Step 1: pre-flight confirms the product is the owner's own; clearance search finds no conflicting mark for "Shelfmark" in its category, the exact-match domain is available, and the social handles are free. Recorded in `fact-sheet.md`. The name proceeds.
3. Step 2: requirements freeze the two lists — changes: name, logo, palette, type, voice, domain, handles; does-not-change: accounts, saved bookmarks, the importer, pricing (there is none — the app is free, and the fact-sheet says so rather than implying a pricing page exists).
4. Step 3: route inventory crawl finds 12 public routes and 3 authenticated routes; the baseline marks the pricing-free landing page, the blog index, and 4 help articles as the organic landing routes. The surface audit finds the old name in: 15 templates, 41 string-catalog entries, 6 email templates, the privacy policy and terms, 1 app-directory listing, the OAuth consent screen, and — the catch of the run — the favicon file and the og image, both still carrying the old wordmark.
5. Step 4: identity spec written (name forms, new wordmark, palette, type, voice notes); `old-new-mapping.md` frozen with 12 route rows and the terminology column (the product's "loops" become "shelves" — a feature rename, recorded as in-scope in `DECISIONS.md` because it changes user-visible vocabulary, not behavior). The rebrand-execution skill's gates pass on both documents.
6. Step 5: tokens replaced, components re-skinned, no layout changes; copy rewritten from the mapping table; naming lint (G-CO-053) catches "loop" surviving in two empty-state strings — fixed at source. Accessibility scan passes on the new palette after one accent color is darkened to meet contrast (G-AC-005, G-EXP-06).
7. Step 6: 6 email templates rebranded and re-authenticated on the new sending domain (G-IN-061, G-IN-064 pass on seed sends); help articles updated and re-screenshotted (G-CX-025); the directory listing and OAuth consent screen are updated, with the listing's provider review noted in the runbook as a dated follow-up.
8. Step 7: terms and privacy regenerated under the new name; G-LG-032 catches the old name in the privacy policy's version-archive header — classified as a legitimate historical occurrence and added to the approved-reuse list with that reason, not edited out of the archive.
9. Step 8: redirect map built — 12 public rows one-to-one, the 3 authenticated routes mapped to their new-domain equivalents, the retired `/pricing` URL (a leftover page with no successor content) answered 410 with the reason on its row. Sitemaps reconciled (G-CO-092); Organization structured data updated to the new name and URL (G-CO-082). The seo-migration skill's gates pass.
10. Step 9: residue scan (G-LG-094) finds one hit — the old name inside a PDF user guide linked from the help center. The guide is regenerated from the rebranded source and the scan re-runs clean over the whole document class. G-SE-001: 0 criticals. G-QA-141 clean.
11. Step 10: user approves the DNS change; new domain live with certificates probed (G-DO-111/112); old domain deployed with the frozen redirect map; G-DO-071 passes on the new domain, and the old domain answers with redirects, not a parked page. Rollback had been rehearsed on staging (G-DO-151).
12. Step 11: live re-fetch of all 15 redirect rows matches the map (G-CO-003); new sitemaps submitted; coverage review log opened against the step 3 baseline (G-CO-005). Announcement email sent from the new domain and the in-product notice published: same account, same bookmarks, new name — and the predictable "is this the same product?" tickets are answered from the mapping table. Done.

---

# technical-seo

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/seo-content/technical-seo/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/seo-content.md`).*

## Rules

1. **CO-001 — The indexable-page contract.** Every page intended for search returns HTTP 200, carries a self-referencing canonical, and is reachable by following links from the site itself. A page failing any leg is a defect to fix, not a ranking mystery to explain.
2. **CO-002 — Server-rendered by default.** Indexable content ships as server-rendered or statically generated HTML. Client-side rendering of indexable content is an exception that must be verified under CO-003, never a default.
3. **CO-003 — Verify the rendered HTML.** JavaScript-dependent content is checked in the rendered HTML (Search Console URL Inspection or an equivalent rendered-DOM fetch), never assumed from source code, view-source, or a local build.
4. **CO-004 — robots.txt discipline.** robots.txt follows RFC 9309 syntax, is served at the host root with HTTP 200, and never blocks the CSS or JavaScript assets that rendering the pages requires. Every change to it is reviewed like a code change.
5. **CO-005 — The promotion indexability diff.** Before every production release, staging and production are diffed on robots.txt, `noindex` (meta and X-Robots-Tag), basic-auth walls, and canonical host. Any staging protection found in production is a release blocker.
6. **CO-006 — One canonical URL per page.** Each page has exactly one canonical URL, stated as an absolute URL that itself returns 200 and is indexable. Parameter, filter, sort, session, and print variants canonicalize to the base URL or carry `noindex`; they are never indexable duplicates competing with it.
7. **CO-007 — Redirect hygiene.** Permanent moves use 301 or 308. Redirects are single-hop wherever the destination is known; a chain longer than two hops is fixed at the source, not documented and left.
8. **CO-008 — Real status codes.** Missing content returns a real 404 or 410. An error page served with HTTP 200 (a soft 404) is a defect, as is redirecting every removed URL to the homepage.
9. **CO-009 — One host, one scheme.** The site canonicalizes to a single host form (www or non-www) over HTTPS. Every other host/scheme combination 301-redirects to it, and canonicals, sitemaps, and internal links use only that form.
10. **CO-010 — The sitemap contract.** The XML sitemap lists only canonical, indexable URLs that return 200, is regenerated when routes change, stays within protocol limits (50,000 URLs / 50 MB per file, sitemap index beyond that), and is referenced in robots.txt. Generation itself belongs to the sitemaps skill; this rule is the contract it must satisfy.
11. **CO-011 — Directive consistency.** robots.txt, meta robots, X-Robots-Tag, and canonicals never contradict each other on the same URL, and no CDN, firewall, or hosting rule blocks search or AI crawlers that robots.txt allows — Google names CDN/hosting-level blocking as a real eligibility failure for its AI features.
12. **CO-012 — Coverage reviewed on a cadence.** Search Console coverage and indexing reports are reviewed on a fixed cadence (monthly at minimum) and the review is logged. Every spike in excluded or error URLs is triaged to a named cause. Reports state eligibility and defects found; they never state or imply a ranking guarantee.

## Checklist

- [ ] Promotion indexability diff is clean: no staging directive in production (G-CO-001).
- [ ] Every indexable URL returns 200 with a self-referencing canonical (G-CO-002).
- [ ] robots.txt is RFC 9309-valid and blocks no render asset (CO-004).
- [ ] Redirect chains are ≤2 hops; permanent moves are 301/308 (G-CO-003).
- [ ] Deleted URLs return a real 404/410 — no soft 404s (CO-008).
- [ ] JavaScript-dependent templates verified in rendered HTML (G-CO-004).
- [ ] Sitemap lists only canonical, indexable, 200 URLs (CO-010).
- [ ] This month's Search Console coverage review is logged, with no ranking guarantee stated (G-CO-005).

<!-- generated from skills/seo-content/web-analytics/SKILL.md (pointer) -->
- **web-analytics** — search and acquisition measurement is set up, audited, or reported: Search Console verification, coverage and performance review, GA4 organic landing-page analysis, and the content decisions that follow from them. This skill owns the search/acquisition slice of measurement. (`skills/seo-content/web-analytics/SKILL.md`; full text in `bundles/seo-content.md`)

<!-- generated from skills/seo-content/content-strategy/SKILL.md (pointer) -->
- **content-strategy** — deciding what content a site will produce, in what order, for whom, and to what end — topic maps, editorial calendars, briefs, and refresh/retire decisions. This skill owns the production system: strategy sets audience, goals, and topic ownership before any drafting starts. (`skills/seo-content/content-strategy/SKILL.md`; full text in `bundles/seo-content.md`)

(`skills/cloning-replication/page-inventory/SKILL.md`; full text in `bundles/cloning-replication.md`)

# rebrand-execution

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/cloning-replication/rebrand-execution/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/cloning-replication.md`).*

## Rules

1. **CL-701 — The rebrand starts from a signed identity decision record.** Before any surface changes, a dated record names: the old and new name (exact spelling, capitalization, and spacing), the new logo files, the new token set handed over from design-system, the approved voice/copy source, the launch date, and the surfaces explicitly out of scope. Work that starts from a chat message, a mood board, or a logo file alone has no authority to change a live product.
2. **CL-702 — Every identity surface is inventoried before the first swap.** The inventory is a written list, built by crawling the product and its repositories, covering at minimum: header/footer and navigation, favicons and app icons, the web-app manifest name and short name, the sender name shown on push notifications and installed-app surfaces, Open Graph and social-card images, structured data (`Organization` name and logo), page titles and meta descriptions, sitemap and robots references to the old name or host, email templates, sender names, and the sending domain (whose authentication records are re-proven under transactional-email and domains-dns when the domain itself changes), transactional and system messages, in-app strings and message catalogs in every locale, error and empty-state copy, legal pages (terms, privacy, imprint, copyright footer), PDF and downloadable assets, app-store listings, social profiles and handles, package and repository names where user-visible, support and help-center branding, and third-party integrations that display the name or logo (payment pages and the statement descriptor customers see on their card statements, OAuth consent screens, embedded widgets). A surface not on the inventory is assumed missed, not assumed unaffected.
3. **CL-703 — The inventory records old value, new value, and owner per surface.** Each inventory row states where the old identity lives (file, template, catalog key, CMS field, or third-party console), the exact replacement value, and who makes the change. Rows whose new value is not yet decided are marked `blocked` and block the swap schedule for that surface — they are never filled in by guesswork at swap time.
4. **CL-704 — URLs, routes, and identifiers do not change for identity alone.** A rebrand changes presentation, not addressing: existing paths, slugs, deep links, API identifiers, anchor IDs, and analytics property IDs stay byte-identical unless a separate, approved migration plan under technical-seo covers them. If the name appears inside a URL, that URL is listed in the inventory as `keep` or as an explicit migration item — never renamed as a side effect of a find-and-replace.
5. **CL-705 — The swap is token- and catalog-driven, never hand-edited per page.** Colors, typography, and logo references change in the design tokens and shared components (per design-system), and name and voice strings change in the message catalogs and shared templates. A value that must be edited in more than one place is first centralized, then changed once. Per-page hand edits are drift by construction and are reverted to the centralized source.
6. **CL-706 — The old name survives only where the record says so.** After the swap, the old name and old logo may remain only in places the decision record explicitly preserves: legal entity names in terms, privacy, contracts, and copyright lines where the registered entity has not changed; historical content (old blog posts, changelogs, press) left as an archive; and redirect or alias configurations kept for continuity. Every surviving instance found after launch maps to one of these recorded exceptions; an unmapped instance is a defect.
7. **CL-707 — Legal identity is checked separately from brand identity.** The brand name and the legal entity name are different facts. Before launch, a named reviewer confirms for each legal surface whether the registered entity, trading name, tax or registration details, and copyright holder actually changed. Brand copy is never copied into a legal surface, and a legal name is never "rebranded" by substitution.
8. **CL-708 — Search surfaces are swapped as data, not as decoration.** Page titles, meta descriptions, Open Graph and Twitter card fields, canonical URLs, sitemap entries, and structured data are updated from the inventory as structured fields and re-validated with the owning skills' checks (technical-seo, social-open-graph, structured-data, sitemaps). The Organization structured-data `name` and `logo` must match the visible brand and the logo file actually served at the declared URL; a logo URL that still serves the old mark is a failed swap, however new the page looks.
9. **CL-709 — The new palette and type pass accessibility checks before launch, not after.** New color pairs and new typography are verified against WCAG 2.2 contrast criteria (1.4.3, 1.4.11) and the design-system contrast gate on the real components that carry them — buttons, links, badges, charts, disabled and error states — before the swap ships. A brand color that cannot be used accessibly gets a documented accessible variant in the token set; body text is never shipped in a failing pair to preserve the palette.
10. **CL-710 — Voice and copy changes follow inclusive-copy, in every locale.** Replacement copy is written and reviewed under inclusive-copy (one glossary term per concept, plain language, no idiom carrying meaning), the new product name is added to the project glossary with its do-not-use variants (old name, wrong capitalization, abbreviations), and every shipped locale is inventoried and swapped — a rebrand that ships in the source locale while other locales still carry the old name and old voice is a partial rebrand and is reported as such, never as launched.
11. **CL-711 — Functional behavior is frozen during the swap window.** The rebrand change set contains identity changes only: no feature work, no flow restructuring, no dependency upgrades ride along. If a functional change is genuinely inseparable from an identity surface, it is split out, named in the inventory, and tested on its own. This freeze is what makes the post-swap regression check (G-CL-704) interpretable.
12. **CL-712 — The swap is rehearsed on staging and launched as one release.** The full inventory is executed once on staging and verified there before production is touched. Production launch is a single release containing the whole in-scope inventory — not a drip of surfaces over days — so that at no point does the live product present two identities as its current state. Deliberately phased rollouts (for example per-locale) are recorded as phases in the decision record, each phase complete in itself.
13. **CL-713 — A rollback keeps the old identity restorable for the launch window.** The pre-swap token set, logo files, catalogs, and templates are preserved as a versioned artifact until the post-launch verification window in the decision record closes. Rollback restores that artifact; nobody reconstructs the old identity from memory, screenshots, or a design file.
14. **CL-714 — Post-launch monitoring compares against the pre-rebrand baseline.** Before launch, baseline snapshots are recorded for the surfaces a rebrand can silently damage: top landing pages' titles and indexation status, sitemap validity, structured-data validity, 404 and redirect behavior on the highest-traffic URLs, and primary-flow completion. After launch these are re-checked against the baseline (G-CL-705); a difference is investigated as a rebrand defect until shown otherwise, not attributed to "normal fluctuation" without evidence.
15. **CL-715 — Third-party surfaces are verified in the third party's own console.** Every integration on the inventory that displays the name or logo — payment provider pages and statement descriptors, OAuth consent screens, app-store listings, social profiles, embedded chat or support widgets — is opened and checked where it actually renders after the change. A change made in the product's own codebase is not evidence that a third-party surface changed.
16. **CL-716 — The rebrand closes with a residue report.** At the end of the verification window, the inventory is re-run as an audit: each row is marked `swapped`, `kept by exception` (naming the CL-706 exception), or `missed`. The report, the surviving-old-name exceptions, and any missed surfaces with their fix dates are recorded in progress.md. A rebrand with no residue report is not closed, however clean the launch looked.

## Checklist

- [ ] A dated decision record names old/new identity, scope, out-of-scope surfaces, and launch date (CL-701).
- [ ] The surface inventory covers rendered, data, catalog, legal, downloadable, and third-party surfaces in every locale, each row with old value, new value, and owner (CL-702, CL-703, G-CL-701).
- [ ] No URL, slug, identifier, or analytics property changed for identity alone; any exception is an approved migration item (CL-704, G-CL-703).
- [ ] The swap was made in tokens, shared components, and catalogs — not hand-edited per page (CL-705).
- [ ] Legal surfaces were confirmed by a named reviewer separately from brand copy (CL-707).
- [ ] Titles, meta, OG fields, sitemap, and Organization structured data carry the new identity and validate (CL-708, G-CL-702).
- [ ] New palette and type passed contrast checks on real components before launch (CL-709).
- [ ] New name is in the glossary with do-not-use variants; all locales swapped or the launch is reported as partial (CL-710).
- [ ] The change set contains identity changes only; functional diffs were split out (CL-711, G-CL-704).
- [ ] Staging rehearsal passed and production launched as one release or as recorded complete phases (CL-712).
- [ ] The pre-swap identity artifact is preserved until the verification window closes (CL-713).
- [ ] Post-launch baseline comparison, third-party checks, and residue report are filed; the rebrand is closed only then (CL-714, CL-715, CL-716, G-CL-705).

# design-system

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/frontend/design-system/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/frontend.md`).*

## Rules

1. **FE-021 — The system is four artifacts.** The token set, the component library, written usage rules, and a changelog. A visual decision that exists only inside one page's code is not part of the system and does not ship as one.
2. **FE-022 — Every decision traces.** Each visual choice on a shipped page traces to a token, a library component, or a documented one-off exception with a written reason. Untraceable styling is drift and is removed or absorbed into the system.
3. **FE-023 — Guidance includes refusal.** Every component's documentation states its purpose, its variants, and at least one "do not use when" case, on the GOV.UK pattern. A component documented only with happy paths will be misused.
4. **FE-024 — Changes are versioned.** A token or component change ships with a changelog entry and a visual-regression pass, never as a silent edit. Consumers of the system learn about change from the changelog, not from a screenshot diff.
5. **FE-025 — Composition varies by role.** Section composition follows content role (hero, proof, dense content, closing): a page where every section shares the same padding, alignment, and loudest element fails system review (DET-VIS-001, DET-VIS-002, DET-VIS-010).
6. **FE-026 — Proof may outrank headings.** Hierarchy serves the message: a metric, a product shot, or a customer quote may be the most prominent element in its section. The heading is not entitled to be loudest by default.
7. **FE-027 — Diagnose before redesigning.** Visual failures are diagnosed against the parameter catalog (WCPM §2, served in this repo by DET-VIS-001…044) and cured with the matching cure rules (CV family) — not by restyling on taste. Clusters are scored as clusters: 3 or more minor tells in one component or section count as one major (WCPM CLU-01…06; enforced by G-DES-02).
8. **FE-028 — The acceptance bar is scored, not felt.** A page passes visual acceptance on the rubric: zero P0 parameters, rubric score ≥ 90, every category ≥ 7, zero F1–F8 auto-fails (WCPM G-DES-01). "Looks fine to me" is not a verdict — human detection of generated design is a near-chance instrument, so the score carries the decision.
9. **FE-029 — Distinctiveness is briefed before building.** Each project opens with a design brief that names its divergence: the visual choices that make this product unlike the template default (WCPM §4, BR- divergence rules and D-MIN minimum thresholds). A brief that could describe any SaaS site is rejected and rewritten.
10. **FE-030 — Imagery belongs to the system.** Photography and illustration follow one documented style and depict the business's real product, place, or people (DET-VIS-023); aspect ratios follow an art-directed grid so subjects survive their crops (DET-VIS-029). Stock or generated imagery depicting nothing real is not a system asset.
11. **FE-031 — The footer is designed.** The footer uses the system's tokens and carries a brand statement, real contact paths, and legal links that resolve — not a generic link grid pasted under the page (DET-VIS-009).

## Checklist

- [ ] The system has all four artifacts, current (FE-021).
- [ ] Sampled elements trace to token, component, or logged exception (G-FE-013).
- [ ] Every component documents a "do not use when" case (FE-023).
- [ ] Token/component changes carry changelog entries (FE-024).
- [ ] DET-VIS cluster review walked at 1440px and 390px (G-FE-011).
- [ ] Rubric acceptance bar met: 0 P0, ≥ 90, categories ≥ 7, zero F1–F8 (G-FE-012).
- [ ] Composition varies by section role; proof may outrank headings (FE-025, FE-026).
- [ ] Imagery depicts the real business in one documented style (FE-030).

# design-tokens

*Condensed for this bundle — Rules + Checklist only. Full skill: `skills/frontend/design-tokens/SKILL.md` (also in `bundles/frontend.md`).*

## Rules

1. **FE-041 — One format, one source.** Tokens are authored once in DTCG-format JSON — every token an object with `$value`, `$type`, and aliases by dot-path — and transformed by Style Dictionary (or Terrazzo) into CSS custom properties and other platform outputs. Hand-edited output files are defects.
2. **FE-042 — Three tiers.** Primitive (raw values) → semantic (roles: `color-action-primary`, `surface-raised`) → component. Theming happens at the semantic tier by overriding the same names; a theme never duplicates the primitive file.
3. **FE-043 — Semantic only in components.** Components reference semantic tokens exclusively. A primitive value, hex code, pixel, or millisecond literal in component styles is a defect found by lint, not by opinion.
4. **FE-044 — Every token is documented.** Each token carries a `$description` naming its role. Retired tokens are marked `$deprecated` with a pointer to their replacement — never silently deleted, so existing code fails loudly instead of drifting.
5. **FE-045 — Scales with named roles.** Elevation, radius, spacing, and duration are scales whose steps have roles (radius: input / card / pill; elevation: flat / card / menu / modal). Values are applied by role — the direct counter to the single-shadow default (DET-VIS-021) and radius scatter (DET-VIS-043).
6. **FE-046 — Pairs pass contrast before they are named.** A semantic foreground/background pair is only admitted to the token set after its WCAG ratio is computed: ≥ 4.5:1 for body text, ≥ 3:1 for large text and non-text indicators — including pairs that sit on tinted or gradient surfaces (DET-VIS-022).
7. **FE-047 — The palette has roles, not a hue.** The color system defines primary, secondary, semantic (success / warning / error), and a neutral ramp as distinct tokens. One accent hue covering every role, semantic states included, fails review (DET-VIS-020).
8. **FE-048 — Gradients are tokens with a reason, or absent.** A gradient exists only as a named token whose description states its brand basis and where it may be used. The violet-blue linear gradient is never a default primary, background, or text treatment (DET-VIS-017, DET-VIS-018).
9. **FE-049 — Dark surfaces are layered, not glowing.** Dark themes are built from layered surface tokens with restrained elevation; colored glow shadows are not an elevation device (DET-VIS-019).
10. **FE-050 — Token changes are reviewed as diffs.** Any change to the token source ships with a diff review and the design-system changelog entry (FE-024); a changed value with no diff review is treated as an accidental edit.

## Checklist

- [ ] Token source is DTCG JSON; outputs regenerate cleanly (G-FE-021).
- [ ] No raw hex/px/ms literals in component or page styles (G-FE-022).
- [ ] Every token carries a `$description` (FE-044).
- [ ] Every semantic text/surface pair computes ≥ 4.5:1 or ≥ 3:1 large (G-FE-023).
- [ ] Palette defines primary, secondary, semantic, and neutral roles (FE-047).
- [ ] Elevation and radius applied by role from their scales (FE-045).
- [ ] Any gradient is a named token with a stated brand basis (FE-048).
- [ ] Token diff reviewed; deprecations point at replacements (G-FE-024).

## Gate criteria digest — every gate this playbook cites

Generated from the owning skills: each cited gate's Check criterion, condensed to its first sentence(s) where long, and its Pass criterion complete and exact. Fail actions and full procedures live in the owning skill and in the department bundles. This digest ships at every rung — it is what makes this bundle the default complete load for the walk (BOOTSTRAP.md step 3).

### clone-ethics (`skills/legal-privacy/clone-ethics/SKILL.md`)

- **G-LG-094 — Brand-residue scan.** Check: grep the rebuild for the source's brand names, trademarked terms, and slogans, and hash-compare shipped media against the harvested-asset set; any hit outside the authorization's explicitly approved reuse list blocks. Pass: zero unapproved residue.

### legal-documents (`skills/legal-privacy/legal-documents/SKILL.md`)

- **G-LG-035 — Counsel-review and live-read check.** Check: confirm a counsel-review record (reviewer, date, version) exists for the current version and each material change, with no version published while in draft status; then read the live privacy notice against the data inventory end to end and exercise each contact and rights route it names. Pass: review records complete, no practice in the inventory missing from the notice or vice versa, every named route answers.
- **G-LG-031 — Document-vs-register diff.** Check: in CI, extract the processor names and data categories named in the privacy notice and diff them against the processor register and the RoPA; repeat for every served locale/surface variant. Pass: zero names or categories present in one source and absent from the other.
- **G-LG-032 — Template-residue lint.** Check: scan the publishable document set for bracketed placeholders (`\[…\]`, `{{…}}`, "Lorem", "TODO"), and for any organization or product name not in the project's approved-names list from the fact-sheet. Pass: zero hits.

### licensing (`skills/legal-privacy/licensing/SKILL.md`)

- **G-LG-051 — CI license scan.** Check: run a source-level scan (ScanCode Toolkit) plus the ecosystem metadata checker (`license-checker`, `pip-licenses`, or `cargo-deny`) over the full tree, including vendored directories; compare every detected SPDX identifier against the policy tiers for the target distribution model. Pass: no forbidden-tier identifier, no unlisted identifier, and no component detected that lacks an inventory row.

### technical-seo (`skills/seo-content/technical-seo/SKILL.md`)

- **G-CO-002 — Route inventory crawl.** Check: automated — crawl the production route inventory and assert, per indexable URL: HTTP 200, self-referencing canonical in the canonical host form, no `noindex`. Pass: 100% of indexable URLs satisfy all three.
- **G-CO-003 — Redirect and status audit.** Check: automated — follow every redirect reachable from internal links and the sitemap; assert chains are ≤2 hops, permanent moves are 301/308, and a sample of deleted URLs returns 404/410, not 200 or a homepage redirect. Pass: all assertions hold.
- **G-CO-001 — Promotion indexability diff.** Check: automated — script fetches staging and production robots.txt plus the response headers and meta robots of the top route templates, and diffs directives and canonical host. Pass: zero staging protections (noindex, Disallow: /, auth wall, staging canonical) present in production.
- **G-CO-005 — Coverage review log.** Check: manual — the monthly Search Console review exists in the project log with excluded/error counts, each spike triaged to a named cause, and no ranking or traffic guarantee stated anywhere in it. Pass: log entry complete for the current month.

### web-analytics (`skills/seo-content/web-analytics/SKILL.md`)

- **G-CO-121 — Tracking-plan diff.** Check: automated — export the live tag/event list (GTM container export or a crawl grep for measurement IDs, e.g. `grep -rhoE "G-[A-Z0-9]{6,}" dist/ | sort -u`, plus the implemented event names) and diff it against the shared tracking plan's entries. Pass: zero live tags or events missing from the plan, and zero plan entries with no live implementation.

### rebrand-execution (`skills/cloning-replication/rebrand-execution/SKILL.md`)

- **G-CL-701 — Inventory completeness gate.** Check: crawl the staging product and grep all repositories, message catalogs (every locale), templates, and CMS exports for the old name and old logo file names; diff the hit list against the inventory. Pass: zero unlisted hits and zero `blocked` rows.
- **G-CL-702 — Residue scan.** Check: after the staging swap, re-run the G-CL-701 grep over code, catalogs, rendered page HTML (including `<title>`, meta, OG/Twitter fields, and JSON-LD), sitemap, email templates, and downloadable assets; fetch the declared Organization logo URL and the favicon and confirm they serve the new mark. Pass: every remaining old-name or old-logo hit maps to a recorded CL-706 exception, and all fetched assets are the new identity.
- **G-CL-703 — URL and search-integrity gate.** Check: diff the production URL set (from the sitemap and a crawl) before and after launch; assert every pre-launch URL still returns its pre-launch status or a single-hop permanent redirect to an approved migration target; re-run the technical-seo indexability checks and the structured-data and sitemaps validations on the top landing pages. Pass: zero unintended URL changes, zero new 404s or redirect chains, canonicals, sitemap, and structured data valid and carrying the new identity.
- **G-CL-704 — Functional regression gate.** Check: run the product's existing critical-flow test suite (or, where none exists, a scripted click-through of the primary flows: sign-up, sign-in, core task, checkout or equivalent, password reset) against staging before and after the swap, with identical test data. Pass: identical results; the only diffs are identity strings and assets named in the inventory.
- **G-CL-705 — Post-launch verification and closure gate.** Check: within the verification window in the decision record, (a) open every third-party surface on the inventory in its own console or live rendering, (b) re-check the CL-714 baseline (titles, indexation, sitemap, structured data, top-URL status codes), (c) confirm the design-system contrast gate result for the new token pairs is on record, and (d) file the residue report. Pass: all four done, baseline differences explained or fixed, residue report complete.

### design-system (`skills/frontend/design-system/SKILL.md`)

- **G-FE-014 — Token and contrast enforcement.** Check: automated — the design-tokens gates run as this skill's enforcement arm: token-literal lint and the semantic-pair contrast script (G-FE-022, G-FE-023). Pass: both green.
- **G-FE-011 — DET-VIS cluster review.** Check: manual — per milestone, walk DET-VIS-001…044 in ID order against full-page screenshots at 1440px and 390px; mark each hit with a screenshot or measured value; apply the cluster rule (3+ minors in one section = 1 major). Pass: zero blockers, zero majors, clusters resolved.
- **G-FE-012 — Rubric acceptance score.** Check: manual scoring against the WCPM G-DES-01 bar — count P0 parameter hits, score the rubric, check every category ≥ 7 and zero F1–F8 auto-fails. Pass: 0 P0, score ≥ 90, all categories ≥ 7, zero auto-fails.

- **G-FE-022 — Literal lint.** Check: automated — a stylelint custom rule (or grep script) fails on hex, px, or ms literals in component and page style files, excluding the token source and generated outputs. Pass: zero hits.

Pass: zero findings.

- **G-IN-061 — Authentication check.** Check: automated — query DNS (`dig +short TXT <sending-subdomain>`, the DKIM selector record, and `dig +short TXT _dmarc.<sending-subdomain>`), then send a test message and assert its `Authentication-Results` header shows SPF, DKIM, and DMARC all passing and aligned with the visible From: domain, on a subdomain separate from the marketing stream. Pass: all three pass and align.
- **G-IN-064 — End-to-end arrival test.** Check: automated in staging — complete the signup and password-reset flows; assert a message row exists with a provider message ID and reaches the delivered state via provider events, and that completing the reset actually changes the credential (the old password fails, the new one works). Pass: both flows arrive and the reset takes effect.

- **G-CO-071 — DNS authentication check.** Check: automated in CI for every sending domain — `dig +short TXT example.com` shows an SPF record, `dig +short TXT selector._domainkey.example.com` returns the DKIM key, `dig +short TXT _dmarc.example.com` returns a DMARC record, and the DMARC domain aligns with the From domain. Pass: all three records present and aligned.
- **G-CO-072 — Seed-send rendering test.** Check: automated — after any journey edit, send the full sequence to seed accounts, capture the rendered messages, and scan them for unrendered tokens: `grep -E '\{\{|}}|undefined|null|NaN' rendered/` returns nothing. Pass: zero token hits on every channel.

- **G-CX-022 — UI-label and link audit (automated).** Check: run a link-check crawl over the whole center (`linkchecker` or the platform's built-in broken-link report) and diff every bolded UI label quoted in article steps against the current release's label inventory. Pass: zero broken links, zero labels absent from the current UI.
- **G-CX-025 — Stale-article sweep.** Check: list all articles whose last-verified date predates the latest UI release touching their flow; assert each is re-verified (date updated after a live walkthrough) or archived. Pass: zero live articles stale past a flow-changing release.

### sitemaps (`skills/seo-content/sitemaps/SKILL.md`)

- **G-CO-091 — Sitemap audit script.** Check: automated — `python3 scripts/sitemap_audit.py --sitemap https://example.com/sitemap.xml` fetches the sitemap (following the index to every shard), requests every listed URL (or a statistically sound random sample above 10,000 URLs), and asserts per URL: HTTP 200, no redirect, canonical tag equal to the listed URL, no `noindex` in meta robots or X-Robots-Tag, host and scheme equal to the canonical host. Pass: zero assertion failures.
- **G-CO-092 — Count reconciliation.** Check: automated — the build compares the generated sitemap's URL count against the route/content inventory count and writes both numbers plus a reason for every excluded inventory item (draft, noindex, redirect) to the build log. Pass: counts reconcile with every difference explained.

Pass: every block parses and carries all required properties.
- **G-CO-082 — Markup-vs-visible diff.** Check: automated — script diffs `aggregateRating`, `price`, `datePublished`/`dateModified`, and `author` values in JSON-LD against the rendered page text for the same sample URLs. Pass: zero fields without an identical visible counterpart (page-external fields checked against fact-sheet.md per CO-172).

- **G-CO-111 — Site-wide tag dump diff.** Check: automated — crawl every public URL, extract all OG and Twitter tags, and diff: og:url must equal the page's canonical URL, og:title/og:description must match the page's own title/topic with no cross-page duplicates across different destinations, og:site_name must equal the current brand name, and all four required properties must be present. Pass: zero mismatches.
- **G-CO-112 — og:image resolution and size check.** Check: automated — request every distinct og:image URL; assert absolute URL, HTTP 200, image content type, and dimensions of 1200×630; flag any image reused across pages outside the recorded fallback list. Pass: every og:image resolves at full share size and reuse matches the fallback record, and every page without one carries the recorded no-image disposition.

- **G-CO-011 — Metadata lint.** Check: automated CI lint over the route inventory — extract every indexable page's `<title>` and meta description and fail on duplicates, missing values, or placeholder strings: `grep -rhoP '(?<=<title>).*?(?=</title>)' dist/ | sort | uniq -d` returns nothing, and the same for descriptions. Pass: zero duplicates, zero missing, zero defaults.
